Thirty-Four Days of Wind

STS-HS12-L4-6501000-HSSCIENG1112-HJD-API-03 • HS Science Engineering Design 11-12 • Model energy, matter, and information flows
Look at the picture. You will answer some questions about it. Press the play button to hear each question. Record your answer for each question. You can listen to your answer and record it again. Click SUBMIT RECORDINGS when you have answered all the questions.
JUST FOR FUN · OPTIONAL
In 1976 a double-hulled canoe called Hōkūleʻa crossed from Hawaiʻi to Tahiti in about thirty-four days with no instruments aboard, no compass, no charts, no radio. The navigator read the wind, the swells, and the stars, and wrote what he read into a log every single day. Kalei, Haruto, and Meli are turning those old entries into a working model of how energy, matter, and information moved through that canoe.
A single log entry records the wind speed, the direction of the water, and the star the navigator steered by. Which one of those three is an information flow rather than an energy or matter flow, and why?
Optional. You do not have to record this one.
